task: Write a due diligence memo on Canva

merged.claim: Canva co-founders and roles: Melanie Perkins (CEO), Cliff Obrecht (COO), Cameron Adams (Chief Product Officer).
Canva was founded in 2013 (1 January 2013 in Perth, per Wikipedia) and is headquartered in Sydney, Australia.

Founder backgrounds: Perkins and Obrecht previously built Fusion Books (2007), an online school-yearbook design business; Adams was formerly a lead designer at Google and joined as technology co-founder after an introduction by Lars Rasmussen.
Kelly Steckelberg joined Canva as CFO in November 2024. She was previously Zoom CFO (through its IPO), CEO of Zoosk, and held finance roles at Cisco; she began her career at KPMG.
Zach Kitschke is Canva's CMO.
Todd Carpenter is Chief Legal Officer & Corporate Development (per Clay dossier, may lag).
Javier Soltero left Canva's operating enterprise role in May 2024 after about six months and returned to an adviser role; he previously held senior roles at Google and Microsoft.

May 2026 departures: growth lead Iain Dowling resigned after eight years and senior engineering director Jonathan Ross leaves at end-May 2026 (AFR). Involuntary termination is not established, and staff job-security concerns were reported.
Head of design Andrew Green (joined October 2018 from SEEK) announced his departure and will remain an adviser. B dates this to April 2026; A lists it among the May 2026 departures.
CTO Brendan Humphreys reportedly departed in May 2026 (reported only, not confirmed elsewhere).

Red flag: leadership continuity risk from 2026 design, growth and engineering departures amid the AI pivot; a common cause is not established. Critical press frames the exits, AI-credits shift, delayed IPO and AI-linked price rises as strain.
October 2015: $15M Series A led by Felicis Ventures with Blackbird and Matrix Partners, at a $165M valuation.
September 2016: $15M round led by Blackbird and Felicis at a $345M valuation.
January 2018: $40M round at a $1B valuation; Sequoia China joined Blackbird and Felicis, and Blackbird's Rick Baker led.
May 2019: $70M raised at a $2.5B valuation.
October 2019: $85M raised at a $3.2B valuation; investors included Bond, General Catalyst, Bessemer, Blackbird and Sequoia China.
June 2020: $60M round at a $6B valuation; Bond and Blackbird were quoted and no single lead was identified.

15 September 2021: $200M round at a $40B valuation led by T. Rowe Price, with Franklin Templeton, Sequoia Capital Global Equities, Bessemer, Greenoaks, Dragoneer, Blackbird, Felicis and AirTree. It is the last primary round, with no new primary money since.
Canva raised about $569M in primary equity across 11 rounds from 2013 to 2021.
August 2023: ~$100M Blackbird secondary sale to Coatue and ICONIQ at a $25.5B valuation.
March-April 2024: ~$1.6B Goldman Sachs-run staff/early-investor secondary sale at ~$26B; trades at $32B in October 2024; over $2B of existing shares sold since 2023, none to the company.

August 2025 employee share sale at a $42B valuation, led by Fidelity with JPMorgan Asset Management participating. It is secondary liquidity rather than a primary raise; final close and proceeds are unverified and share count is undisclosed.
2026 investor marks are below the $42B employee-sale price: T. Rowe Price implied $38.2B, Franklin Templeton $39.3B, Blackbird $34.9B as of 30 June 2026 (Forbes Australia).
Canva's own independent valuation for its August 2026 employee share issue fell ~20% year over year to $31B.

Canva is private with no IPO filing. COO Cliff Obrecht told Bloomberg in November 2025 an IPO will come in the next 'couple of years' (reportedly 2027), and Canva ruled out an Australian listing in September 2025.

Business model: freemium subscription (Free, Pro for individuals, per-person Business, sales-led custom-priced Enterprise); eligible schools/K-12 and nonprofits get premium features free; originally drag-and-drop design, with print and video added over time.
Product scope: Visual Suite covering presentations, docs, whiteboards, video, websites, spreadsheets, email and social, with Canva AI embedded across workflows.
Canva Enterprise launched in May 2024 alongside Work Kits, Courses and AI capabilities.

Enterprise features and go-to-market: API access, two-way DAM sync (Bynder, Widen, Brandfolder), Salesforce, HubSpot, LinkedIn, Marketo and Eloqua integrations; resellers SoftBank and CDW, agency Designit and consultancy Deloitte.
Canva operates in 190+ countries and 100+ languages, with Canva AI in 16 languages across 31 locales.
Most of Canva's business is from North America; lower-priced subscriptions are offered in markets such as Pakistan, Uruguay, Morocco and Jamaica.
Localization push: 700,000+ non-English templates and 2.3M local elements added in six months; in Japan, a partnership with Irasutoya added 20,000+ illustrations.
Group subsidiaries/brands include Pixabay, Pexels, Serif (Affinity), Kaleido, Leonardo.AI, Smartmockups, Flourish, Cavalry, MangoAI, Simtheory and Ortto.

Acquisitions: Zeetings (2018), Pixabay and Pexels (2019), Kaleido.ai and Smartmockups (2021), Flourish (2022), Serif/Affinity (~$380M, March 2024), Leonardo.AI (2024), MagicBrief (June 2025), Cavalry and MangoAI (February 2026), Simtheory and Ortto (April 2026).

February 2025 corporate reorganisation: a new Delaware company, Canva, Inc., became ultimate holding company and the former parent became Canva Australia Holdings Pty Ltd; ASIC says the Australian group restructured after 2024.
ATO class ruling CR 2025/35 (issued 28 May 2025) covers scrip-for-scrip roll-over for stock options in the Delaware restructure.
Canva claims 265M+ monthly active users (up 20% in 2025) and 31M+ paid users at end-2025.
Canva's 2025 year-in-review cites 260M monthly users in 2025.
Canva claims $4B ARR at end of 2025 (COO Cliff Obrecht).
Sacra estimates end-2025 ARR of $4B, up 43% from $2.8B at end of 2024.
B2B business (companies with 25+ seats) reached $500M ARR, up 100%.
Canva reported 2025 revenue of $3.5B (unaudited company claim); it also claimed it remained profitable with $3.5B annualized revenue (4 November 2025), with net income and margins not quantified.
Reuters reported annualized revenue of $3.3B during the August 2025 employee share sale; Canva separately said it had surpassed $3.4B annualized revenue.
FY2022 financials: revenue up 57% to $962M, statutory loss of $222M driven by $482M employee-benefit expense, cash up to $420M, and a $260M profit excluding share-based payments.
Profitability claims: Canva claims nine years of free-cash-flow profitability and $1.47B cash at end of June 2026 (Sacra says 7 years). Profitability cannot be verified from filed accounts.
Canva claims use by 95% of the Fortune 500, and by thousands of companies via Canva Enterprise.
Named enterprise customers: FedEx, Salesforce, Expedia, Airbnb, Reddit, DocuSign, Zoom and Keller Williams (varies by source).
Customer case metrics (company-reported): FedEx deployed across 1,400 teams in 45 countries; DocuSign saved $300,000 in design hours.
Salesforce case study (company-published): 140+ social accounts, 22 regions, 18 languages, 63% increase in design production and 66% lower cost per design.

Education: Canva claims 100M teachers, students and education leaders use it (2025 year-in-review; 100M reiterated 5 October 2026) and is expanding email-less student accounts. This is not equivalent to paid growth.
Canva's AI mini-apps and website builder tool has 10M+ monthly active users (company claim).
Canva is integrated with ChatGPT and Claude: 26M+ conversations with the Canva app on ChatGPT by October 2025, and a claimed top-10 referred domain from ChatGPT.
Print partnerships with FedEx Office (June 2020) and Office Depot (July 2020).
Product releases: Visual Suite 2 (Sheets, Code, chatbot) on 10 April 2025; Canva AI 2.0 research preview with agentic tools in April 2026; offline mode in August 2026.

Red flag: in July/August 2026 Canva cut its 2026 revenue growth forecast from 30% to 20% because of high AI serving costs, with product rollouts delayed while architecture is rebuilt. CEO Perkins said cost per AI task fell nearly 90% since Canva AI 2.0 launched, but users create three times as many designs.
Pricing backlash: Canva Teams prices rose steeply with genAI features (five-person annual plan from about $120 to $300 then $500) in September 2024, drawing customer backlash.

Canva reversed/softened the price hikes: in October 2024 it kept early adopters' original pricing and promised advance notice of changes, and legacy pricing was restored for small-business and education customers.

May 2019 data breach: profile data for up to 139M users (137.5M per a secondary source) accessed on 24 May 2019, including names, emails and password hashes; partial payment-card files viewed with no evidence of theft; ~4M passwords decrypted and shared online, with unchanged passwords reset on 12 January 2020.

UpGuard (9 June 2025): a My Jedai AI-chatbot database exposed survey responses tied to 571 Canva Creator email addresses; remediated after notification; third-party exposure, not a direct Canva breach.

ASIC: four Australian Canva companies (Canva Pty Ltd, Canva Operations, Canva Trading, Fusion Books) each paid A$198,000 (total A$792,000) in infringement notices for allegedly failing to lodge FY2024 financial reports by 30 April 2025. The report was lodged 27 March 2026, payment is not an admission of liability, and Canva Australia Holdings lodged its FY2025 reports on time on 30 April 2026.

Delhi High Court on 28 January 2026 dismissed Canva's appeal against an interim patent injunction restricting its Present and Record feature in India, upholding INR 50 lakh security for past use; findings are prima facie with merits left for trial.
DigiMedia Tech, LLC v. Canva Pty Ltd, a patent-infringement action in E.D. Texas filed 18 August 2025, was not shown as terminated in the retrieved docket.

September 2026: competing Los Angeles Superior Court suits between Canva and music-rights contractor Crunch Digital. Canva alleges confidential-data disclosure; Crunch alleges breach and non-payment (allegations only).
Canva reportedly settled an unfair dismissal case brought by a senior engineer (AFR, 10 April 2024; secondary citation).

Late March/early April 2025 AI-linked layoffs: 10 of 12 technical-writing staff were made redundant. Canva described it as engineers taking ownership of documentation, and employees said they had been reassured AI would not cause layoffs.
Headcount: 5,000-5,500 employees in 2024, with about 1,000 added that year (1,128 new hires in a year; UK team scaled from 100 to 250+).
Canva claimed its global team expanded nearly 40% (2025 CNBC Disruptor announcement); comparison period and absolute headcount not specified.

Glassdoor rating of 3.8/5 from 904 reviews (69% recommend, 86% CEO approval, 61% positive outlook; senior management and career opportunities 3.1, diversity and inclusion 4.1). Reviews praise coworkers, benefits and learning but cite favoritism, bureaucracy, churn and inconsistent leadership.

Another Glassdoor snapshot shows Canva at 4.1/5 (384 reviews in last 6 months; career opportunities 3.1, work/life balance 3.4, comp and benefits 3.5, culture 3.8), citing favouritism and a leadership-staff disconnect.

Other review sites: Indeed 4.3/5 from 32 reviews; Trustpilot 4.0/5 from 7,884 reviews (criticism of unintuitive editing, slow support, print alignment); BBB shows 171 complaints in three years and 77 in the last 12 months.
Canva's acquisition of Affinity (Serif) sparked concern and protest among parts of the Affinity user community on Reddit.
